thesis: Wax that never quite decides: blobs swell, stretch, pinch off and merge because heat from below makes them buoyant and the top cools them heavy again, lit from within like a small sunset in a glass.
job: open the page and see a lamp, already running, wax already moving
watch blobs rise slowly, stretch a neck, pinch off, drift, cool, sink, merge into the pool
switch the lamp on and off (cold wax sits as a lump in the base, warms up, then lifts off)
turn the heat up or down and see speed and number of blobs change
pick a wax and liquid colour combination
poke or drag the wax with the pointer, add a blob by click
reset, keyboard use, phone width, reduced motion

principles: density drops with heat so warm wax rises
wax cools at top and sinks
viscous, laminar: no splashes, no bounce
surface tension rounds everything and pulls necks into drops
tricks: fake it with metaballs: sum of r^2/d^2 fields over a threshold
give each blob a temperature value that rises near bottom and falls near top, buoyancy = temperature minus mid
damp velocity heavily so motion is syrupy
tests: do blobs ever bounce like balls
does a neck form before a blob splits
is the pool at the bottom connected and wobbling

principles: render field at low resolution then upscale for free softness
steps: compute field per pixel on a small offscreen grid
shade by field gradient for fake volume
tricks: field grid 1/3 to 1/4 resolution, ImageData, putImageData then drawImage scaled with smoothing
gradient of field gives a normal for highlight
colour by field strength gives hot core and cool rim
WebGL shader is faster but 2D canvas works from file without fuss

principles: silhouette is the icon: tapered glass, metal cap, metal base
chrome and brushed brass read as warm lamp hardware
tricks: a bright vertical specular strip on the glass left
inner glow from the bulb pools at the bottom of the liquid
base throws coloured light onto the surface it sits on
tests: does it glow in a dark room

principles: it is a toy: direct manipulation beats panels
controls tucked and small so the lamp is the page
every control changes the lamp visibly at once
tricks: real switch on the lamp base itself
heat slider labelled cool to hot
remember nothing needed; state in memory
tests: does each control change something visible within a second

principles: single file, inline css and js
tricks: devicePixelRatio cap
pause on hidden tab
prefers-reduced-motion slows down not freezes
aria-pressed on toggles

principles: luminous: wax is the brightest thing, liquid is a dim tint
room is dark so the lamp is the light source
complementary pairs: orange wax in deep magenta, green wax in teal, pink in violet
steps: add hot core lighter than rim
tricks: screen/lighter blending for glow
radial gradient halo behind the lamp
slight vignette
tests: wax contrast against liquid is obvious
does it still glow on a phone

kinds.name: classic Astro lamp
kinds.what: tapered glass on chrome base, orange wax in magenta liquid, in a dark room

kinds.name: full-screen ambient lamp
kinds.what: the metaball field fills the whole viewport as a screensaver

kinds.name: tabletop lamp scene
kinds.what: lamp on a desk with wall glow and reflection

kinds.name: neon / rainbow wax lamp
kinds.what: multi-colour blobs that shift hue as they rise

descriptions: glass is a truncated cone, narrow top about 45 to 55% of the bottom width
cap is a small rounded dome and a ring
base is a flared bell wider than the glass
behaviors: blobs near each other merge by a bridge
a rising blob stretches its tail
a blob that touches the pool melts into it

descriptions: a full rise takes 20 to 60 s
velocity damped to a creep, 5 to 25 px/s
behaviors: temperature rises within 15% of bottom and falls near top
lamp off: temperature decays, all wax settles to pool in about 10 s

descriptions: wax core near-white yellow to saturated orange rim
liquid dark violet to magenta, brighter at bottom near bulb
behaviors: light pools on table and wall

descriptions: each palette is wax core, wax rim, liquid top, liquid bottom, glow
behaviors: swatch click changes the lamp instantly, colours ease over about a second
pointer pushes nearby blobs away or pulls them
click on empty liquid drops a new small blob up to a cap of 16
space toggles power, arrow keys change heat, number keys pick palette

descriptions: labels short, quiet, lower-case or small caps, no marketing copy
behaviors: status line reads off, warming, flowing

anti_keywords.instead: heavy damping, necks and merges, nothing rebounds
true metaball field with a threshold so blobs bridge

anti_keywords.not: a control panel dominating the page
anti_keywords.instead: controls small on and under the lamp, the lamp is huge and glowing
dark room where the lamp is the light source

anti_keywords.not: static decoration with a fake toggle
anti_keywords.instead: power, heat and colour all change simulation state

checks: Would a stranger say lava lamp in one glance, from silhouette alone?
Do blobs actually merge and pinch off?
Does power off settle the wax and power on warm it up?
Does heat visibly change speed and count?
Do palette swatches recolour at once?
Does poke / click change the wax?
Does it work at 375px and without console errors?
